blockers.summary: The nullboot maintainer (juliank) objected to individual patch uploads. He wants the fix released as a full 0.6.1 SRU, or possibly a 0.5.4, and said boot loader uploads should not come from people outside the boot team. The debdiffs therefore conflict with the maintainer's release plan.

The upstream fix is in the unreleased 0.6.1. The 0.6.0 release includes large secboot library changes that need testing. The cherry-picked patch has not been shown to apply or work on the jammy and noble versions, so the debdiffs may not match what actually gets released.

The debdiffs do not follow packaging conventions. The patch file name, the changelog format with the LP bug number and d/p entry, and the use of the original upstream patch headers (DEP-3) were all queried, and there is no sign these were fixed.

The test plan is a stress loop of 100 reinstalls on an Azure CVM, and the bug is intermittent. It has no stated pass criteria, no verification that the fix was tested on each release, and no regression testing of the other nullboot behaviour.
It is unclear whether nullboot needs a package-specific SRU policy entry. A reviewer asked whether this should be documented, and nobody has answered.
The bug has had no progress since September. The fix depends on a 0.6.1 upload that is not yet scheduled.

The reviewer's one blocking packaging nit is unaddressed: the patch authored by Jorge has 'Origin: backport' where it should be 'Origin: upstream'. No later comment shows a fix.

No resolute SRU upload has been confirmed as accepted into resolute-proposed, and no PPA build has been linked. The reviewer asked for a PPA build twice. The only fixed upload so far is the tenacious one, and that is now proposed for reversion.

The author proposes reverting the fix in tenacious (and dropping stonking) because OpenSSL 4 has no engine support. SRU policy normally wants the fix in the development release first, so this leaves the resolute SRU's status in the devel series unclear.

The reviewer's requests on the bug text are not shown as addressed. The Impact section should say it affects resolute only, because wpa_supplicant registers an engine that OpenSSL 4 no longer supports. The test plan needs the full 'apt install' dependency list. The OpenSSL change that caused the regression should be linked.

The reviewer could not confirm that noble and jammy are unaffected. They also run OpenSSL 3.x with engine and provider support, and no one has linked the regressing OpenSSL commit or said whether those releases are affected.

A user reported that after an engine loads a TPM key once, libtss2-esys cannot create RSA keys in the same process (esys 'Could not create rsa key'), so reconnects may fail. The user later said this was only an unverified LLM hypothesis, and repeated connections were never tested with the patch.
The reviewer's two optional packaging nits are open: keep d/p/series in upstream order, since 6bde508 depends on 5894be2, and use the full commit hash in the upstream URL.
